newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT: Paribas cautious on Indian stocks.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT: Paribas cautious on Indian stocks.

text.p: Paribas Capital Markets on Friday urged investors to be cautious on Indian stocks if Bombay's benchmark stocks index touched 3900-4000 points.
The index ended 17.79 points higher at a provisional 3823.51 on Friday.

"With the resolution of the political crisis the market has turned bullish again. We do not think, though, that much upside potential is left in the market, and investors may wish to book profits if the BSE index crosses 3900," strategist Rupa Bose said in a note to investors.
"We urge caution if the market rises to 3900-4000."
Disappointing 1996/97 (April-March) earnings announcements from leading Indian firms expected during the ongoing reporting season from April to June was an immediate concern, Bose said.
"Our immediate concerns relate to the bad news likely in the results of many stocks this season," she said.

"Much of this is expected but some investors will always be optimists, and it is unlikely that all the bad news has been factored in already -- especially as the market has focused more on the positives of the budget and the political crisis resolution."
The Congress party triggered a political crisis last month when it withdrew its make-or-break support for United Front, prompting a confidence vote that former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda lost.
New Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral won the trust vote earlier this week after Congress resumed its fickle backing.
Analysts say the 1997/98 federal budget -- held hostage to the political crisis -- is likely to be passed by parliament without major amendments.

Bose said longer-term concerns included a recent slowdown in industrial production which had dragged on longer than analysts' expected and which could result in lowered corporate forecasts for 1997/98.
She said a rise in Bombay's stocks index could result in profit-booking and a possible oversupply of fresh paper.
"If the market goes to 3900-4000 levels, we would expect some profit taking," she said.

"We also think that any sustained interest at or above these levels will attract companies interested in raising equity while the opportunity exists, even if the projects they wish to invest in are delayed."
The main positive was the easing of liquidity which was pulling real interest rates lower and making equity attractive relative to debt, Bose said.
